chunks: From him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Umar ibn Uthman, from al-Husayn ibn Khalid, who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him): 'Is it permissible to eat the meat of an elephant?' He said, 'No.' I asked, 'Why?' He said, 'Because it is a mixed breed (or has mixed features), and Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has forbidden the 'amsakh (mixed breeds) and the meat of that which is mixed in its forms.'
ai.seo_question: Why is elephant meat considered haram in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Hasan (peace be upon him) ruled that elephant meat is haram because it is considered 'muthlah' (possessing mixed or distinct features), resembling the 'amsakh' (mixed breeds) whose meat is forbidden by Allah. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle of extending prohibitions from specific Quranic mentions to analogous creatures based on shared physical characteristics. The classification underscores the importance of zoological taxonomy in determining the permissibility of game animals within Islamic dietary laws.
